questions.q: What are the four interior empires the summary says must stay balanced?
a: Mindset, Heartset, Healthset and Soulset
Mindset, Skillset, Toolset and Network
Body, Mind, Spirit and Community
Health, Wealth, Love and Purpose
questions.why: Lesson 2 names these four empires and ties each to mental, emotional, physical and spiritual health.

questions.q: Why does the summary say the early morning suits deep focus?
a: The prefrontal cortex quiets and calming brain chemicals rise
Memory centers become more active before dawn
Cortisol peaks and supplies extra energy
The mind replays the previous day's problems
questions.why: Lesson 1: with fewer distractions and a quieter prefrontal cortex, focus and mood both improve.

questions.q: Which three activities make up the 20/20/20 formula?
a: Exercise, reflection and learning
Reading, journaling and planning
Meditation, breakfast and review
Stretching, news and email
questions.why: Lesson 3 splits the first hour into movement, reflection or meditation, and growth.

questions.q: What does the summary say sweating does for the brain and body?
a: It lowers cortisol and releases a brain-repairing factor
It raises dopamine and sharpens short-term memory
It increases serotonin and improves sleep
It replaces the need for a morning meditation
questions.why: Lesson 3 says sweat cuts cortisol and triggers BDNF, which helps build new neural pathways.

questions.q: Why does waking at 5 a.m. let you accomplish more, per the summary?
a: Your attention has not yet been consumed by distractions
Your willpower is naturally highest at dawn
Your body needs less sleep than most people think
Your goals feel clearer before others wake up
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes mental bandwidth filling up with media and chatter as the day goes on.
